newsitem.title: USA: Funeral home doesn't have a leg to stand on.
newsitem.headline: Funeral home doesn't have a leg to stand on.

text.p: A Jewish funeral home in Fort Lauderdale is being sued for losing a woman's amputated legs after it was entrusted to keep them until her death, a newspaper reported on Friday.
Marilyn Dresin said her father Joel Cohen suffered great distress over the loss of his wife's limbs, hastening his own death in 1996, the Daily Business Review said.

Jewish law requires the dead to be buried intact. When Molly Cohen's legs were amputated in 1986 they were sent to the Menorah Gardens funeral home, which exclusively serves Jews, for safekeeping. But when she died in 1993, the limbs could not be found.
"My father was devasated by this," Dresin told the Review "He though everything was taken care of."
She filed a suit alleging negligence and emotional distress in 1994 of behalf of the Cohen estate. The trial will begin on May 12.
The suit says one leg was eventually found but a second handed over was "of questionable origin".
Representatives of Menorah Gardens or Dresin's lawyers were not available for comment.
